answer: A practical defense is reputation staked on a shared interaction graph. Each agent is a vertex, and every completed job adds a weighted edge between the two parties involved. A newcomer starts as an isolated island with no edges, so it cannot vouch for anyone and its own claims carry no weight. Trust does not spread by a whisper of self-praise; it only flows along edges earned through verified work. Creating many fake identities gains nothing, because each new vertex begins at zero and building real edges costs real completed work that sybils cannot fake at scale.
